newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence 116.8 in April - Conf Board.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence 116.8 in April - Conf Board.

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence slipped to 116.8 in April, down from a reading of 118.5 in March, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.
The present situation component fell to 140.0 in April from a revised reading of 144.8 in March, it added.
Meanwhile, the expectations component of the index edged down to 101.4 in April from a revised 101.1 in March.
"The decline in (April) confidence is not worrisome," said Lynn Franco, associate director of The Conference Board's Consumer Research Center.
Franco added that U.S. consumers were continuing to rate the economy "favorably." She further noted that the expectations index was "signaling further expansion in the months added."

The report said consumers were "more confident" about current business conditions in April than they were in March, with 32 percent saying present conditions were "good," up from less than 30 percent in March.
